name: Combined instrument transformer
summary: Single unit housing a current transformer and voltage transformer for each phase, typical of MV and HV metering points.
description: A combined instrument transformer places a CT and a VT in one insulated housing for each phase. It saves space and foundations at outdoor HV metering points and appears in MV metering units where the supply authority needs both current and voltage for a billing meter.

On a single-line diagram the CT and VT symbols are drawn together with a boundary showing they share one housing. The boundary does not change ratios or classes, which are still stated separately for the current and voltage parts.
readingNotes: Read the CT and VT ratings separately.
Check sealing and access requirements for revenue metering.
distinction: A combined instrument transformer houses a CT and VT together; separate units are drawn and specified independently.
